title: TaskNotes recurrence parity corpus
description: Two files describe this corpus. `corpus.jsonl` is NDJSON: one `case` object per line, sorted by `id`, keys sorted alphabetically, no trailing blank line beyond the final newline. `manifest.json` is a single `manifest` object. Both are produced by packages/tasks-for-obsidian/scripts/build-recurrence-corpus.ts, which drives `shouldShowRecurringTaskOnDate` from @tasknotes/model (wrapping rrule.js) over a fixed 3652-day window. NDJSON is deliberate: Prettier infers no parser for `.jsonl`, so the generated bytes survive the repository formatter unchanged.

case.description: One rule under test and the exact set of dates on which the TypeScript engine reports an occurrence.

id.description: Stable, sortable identifier: a four-digit ordinal, the group, and a slug of the rule string.

group.description: Which input family produced this case.

source.description: `harvested` = a real rule string found in this repository. `generated` = a well-formed grid combination. `edge` = a malformed, contradictory, or hostile input.

note.description: Why this case exists, and any surprising engine behaviour it pins down.

recurrence.description: The rule string exactly as it would appear in a task's `recurrence` frontmatter field. May be empty, malformed, or carry an embedded `DTSTART:`.

scheduled.description: The task's `scheduled` value. First DTSTART fallback when the rule embeds no `DTSTART:`. May carry a time component, of which only the date part is used.

dateCreated.description: The task's `dateCreated` value. Second DTSTART fallback, consulted only when `scheduled` is absent.

outcome.description: `expanded`: the engine reports an occurrence exactly on the dates in `occurrences`. `always`: the engine FAILS OPEN and reports an occurrence on EVERY date, because the rule is empty or unparseable — an implementation that returns false here makes tasks silently vanish. Note the third behaviour is not a separate outcome: when no DTSTART can be resolved the engine fails CLOSED, which appears as `expanded` with an empty `occurrences`.

occurrences.description: Ascending, unique dates inside [manifest.windowStart, manifest.windowEnd] on which `shouldShowRecurringTaskOnDate` returns true. Empty when `outcome` is `always`, since that answer is true on every date and listing it would just restate the window.

occurrenceCount.description: `occurrences.length`, except when `outcome` is `always`, where it is `manifest.windowDays`.

firstOccurrence.description: First date of the raw whole-window expansion, or null when it is empty. Present even for `always` cases, where it describes the second entry point rather than the fail-open answer.

lastOccurrence.description: Last date of the raw whole-window expansion, or null when it is empty.

finiteInstanceCount.description: `getFiniteRecurringInstanceCount`. Null for rules with no COUNT/UNTIL, and also null for an UNTIL that precedes DTSTART — that case is null, not 0.

generatorDayCount.description: Distinct dates returned by `generateRecurringInstances` over the same window. This is a SECOND entry point in the same model and it does NOT always agree with `shouldShowRecurringTaskOnDate`: for an empty `recurrence` the show-check returns true on every date (`outcome: always`) while this generator returns nothing at all. Recorded so the divergence stays visible.

nextUncompletedScheduledAnchor.description: `getNextUncompletedOccurrence` evaluated at `manifest.anchorDate` with the default `scheduled` recurrence anchor, or null.

nextUncompletedCompletionAnchor.description: The same call with `recurrence_anchor: "completion"`, or null.

manifest.description: Sidecar summary of `corpus.jsonl`. Flat and scalar-only so Prettier leaves the formatting alone.

anchorDate.description: The fixed 'today' the corpus is built around. Never a wall clock.

failOpenProbeDate.description: The date used to classify fail-open behaviour: strictly before every DTSTART the corpus can resolve, so a true answer there can only come from the engine's catch-all.
